reason: VALUE fails; FEASIBILITY is mostly OK but the gate is weak. (1) There is no validated direction to extrapolate. exp71's own in-sample proxy shows GT hits 86/88 for both teacher and student, and detection counts moved only 0.995/1.007 (_dl/exp71_secft_all/exp71_train_log.json detection_proxy). The weight delta carries no measured gain, so k=2 doubles an unvalidated, mostly noise-like step. (2) The cited literature works against it on unseen embryos. WiSE-FT (arXiv 2109.01903) shows that moving past the fine-tuned end loses OOD robustness; its fix is interpolation (alpha < 1). exp71 was trained on all 199 train videos, so k=2 amplifies in-sample fit exactly where we need transfer. ExPO (arXiv 2404.16792) is LLM alignment scored by reward models, with no dense-detection or tracking evidence. Local analogs also point down: the head-shift scale s = 1.33 was worse by 1.7-2.6% on both embryos (I-035, CONTEXT l.2033), and model swaps on LB are 0 for 5. (3) The claim that 'the bias cancels, so k scales only the shape' covers detect_head only. decoder_blocks.1 and unet.head also feed the secondary edge features (edge-logit weight 0.15 plus edge-feature TTA, exp72 log l.130-133), so linking drifts 2x as well. (4) Weight-space linearity does not carry through to the metric. The score moves in discrete node and division events (~0.0015-0.0023 display each, R15-A1 (3)), so P(k=2 >= 0.955 | exp72 UP) ~0.5 is too high; ~0.2-0.3 is honest. (5) The '0.954 with an attributable rise' branch is mostly unobservable. exp72 = K2 + secswap without fm45, and our best unrounded is exp70b (K2 + fm45 UP), or probe 45/46 if either rises tonight. exp72 must beat those to show any UP, and if exp75 is submitted in the same 00:05Z window, a rise inside the 0.954 bin cannot be assigned to either file. The marginal chance that N1 lifts our best public display is ~0.03-0.05, not 0.10. (6) Feasibility: the build is byte-identical when off (finals untouched, secswap guard) and cheap (CPU plus one ~0.5 GPU-h dummy), and the schedule fits (exp72 scores ~07:30Z 28 Sep, N1 ~15:30Z). But the dummy clips are TRAIN clips, in-sample for exp71 (log l.139-140), so no honest lab gate exists, which R8 requires. It is past the R8 cutoff, needs a new user OK, and takes a 28/29 Sep slot from exp75, exp74 or the exp73 rungs, which have better odds.
fix: Do not build tonight; put N1 on the post-deadline list. Its only defensible form is narrow. Pre-register now, before exp72 scores, that N1 is considered only if exp72 DISPLAYS >= 0.955; drop the '0.954 attributable' branch. Use k = 1.5, not 2 (half the overshoot). Only then write the weights on CPU: assert that exactly the 10 keys differ, all values are finite and the BN running stats are unchanged. Then create biohub-secft-x2-v1 with model.weight_sha256 set, run the dummy with the exp72 gates plus the requirement that the node and fork deltas have the same sign as exp72's and stay <= 2x exp72's, and ask the user for an explicit OK naming N1. Never make it a final: public-only, class C.
realistic_gain: Public: P(N1 raises our best display) ~0.03-0.05; E[delta public] ~ +0.0001 (range -0.004..+0.002; the retrain family's downside tail is large). Private: 0 as a public-only file; negative in expectation if it were ever made a final (extrapolation away from the pretrained end on unseen embryos). Cost: ~30 min CPU, ~0.5 GPU-h dummy, 1 slot on 28-29 Sep, 1 user OK.
